title: Beef and Root Vegetable Stew
subtitle: A rich British braised beef stew with carrots, parsnips and potatoes
excerpt: Slow-braised beef with root vegetables in a deep, wine-enriched gravy. The beef should be falling apart and the sauce thick enough to coat a spoon. This is proper cold-weather cooking.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from classic British beef stew preparations.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the potatoes (they turn grainy on freezing). Add freshly cooked potatoes when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well in a large stockpot or casserole. The flavour improves the next day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The stew tastes better the next day. Cool, refrigerate and reheat gently on the hob or in a 160 C oven.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 140 C. Low and slow is what makes the beef tender.

content.text: The key to a good stew is browning the beef properly before any liquid goes in. This builds the Maillard flavour that becomes the foundation of the whole dish. Do not rush it: cook the beef in batches so it fries rather than steams. The low, slow braise in the oven then converts the collagen in tougher cuts to gelatin, which gives the gravy its body and silkiness.

items.prepNote: braising beef such as shin or chuck, cut into 4 cm chunks

content.text: Preheat the oven to 160 C (fan 140 C). Pat the beef chunks completely dry with kitchen paper: moisture prevents browning. Season generously with salt and pepper, then toss in the plain flour to coat evenly.

Brown the beef in batches. Heat the oil in a large, oven-safe casserole or heavy saucepan over high heat until shimmering. Add the beef in a single layer, not touching. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes without moving until deeply browned underneath. Turn and brown the other sides. Remove to a plate. Repeat with the remaining beef. Do not crowd the pan: steam traps and the beef will not colour.

Cook the vegetables. Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion and celery to the same pan and cook for 8 minutes until softened, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomato puree and stir for 2 minutes.

Build the braise. Return the browned beef to the pan. Pour in the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce. Add the thyme, rosemary and bay leaves. The liquid should come about halfway up the beef. Bring to the boil, then skim any foam.

Braise in the oven. Transfer to the oven (or keep on the lowest hob setting with a tight lid). Cook for 1 hour 30 minutes. Add the carrot, parsnip and potato chunks, pushing them into the liquid. Return to the oven for another 45 minutes to 1 hour, until the beef is completely tender and falls apart when pressed with a spoon.

Finish the gravy. Remove the thyme stalks, rosemary and bay leaves. Taste the sauce and season. If the gravy is thinner than you like, simmer the stew on the hob over medium heat, uncovered, for 10 to 15 minutes to reduce. Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread or on top of mashed potato.

items.symptom: Beef is tough after 2 hours of cooking
items.cause: The braise temperature was too high, or the cut of beef used was too lean.
items.fix: The oven must be low: 160 C conventional, 140 C fan. A lean cut like sirloin will never become tender this way; use a collagen-rich cut such as shin, chuck or brisket. Return to the oven and continue cooking; it will eventually soften.

items.symptom: Gravy is thin and watery rather than rich and coating
items.cause: Too much stock was added, or the beef was not floured before browning.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered on the hob for 15 to 20 minutes to reduce. Next time, flour the beef well before browning: the flour thickens the sauce as it braises.

items.cause: The beef was not properly browned, losing the depth that browning creates.
items.fix: Add a splash more Worcestershire sauce and check the salt level. A little soy sauce also deepens the savouriness without tasting Asian. Next time, brown the beef until very dark before adding any liquid.

items.symptom: Potatoes have turned mushy and dissolved
items.cause: The potatoes were added too early and have over-cooked.
items.fix: Use a waxy potato variety (such as Charlotte or Desiree) which holds together better. Add them no more than 45 minutes before serving.
